learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of combinational and sequential logic networks, state machines, and memories.
Knowledge of the architecture of programmable digital circuits like PLDs and CPLDs.
Knowledge and understanding of embedded systems and microprocessors.
Knowledge and understanding of the VHDL language for hardware description.
Knowledge of using CAD for VHDL code synthesis and simulation.
Knowledge and understanding of microcontroller characteristics and programming methods.
Ability to analyze and synthesize combinational digital networks and state machines.
Ability to describe simple digital circuits in VHDL.
Ability to independently use CAD for VHDL synthesis and simulation (Quartus Prime, Modelsim), and for writing microcontroller code in laboratory activities (STM32CubeIde).
Ability to write microcontroller code for simple real-time applications.
Ability to independently make simple design choices for the synthesis of digital circuits and microcontroller applications.
Ability to correctly describe the design of a digital circuit on CPLD and/or microcontroller.
Ability to independently find technical documentation on digital electronic devices.

syllabus_topics: Programmable Digital Circuits: CPLD and FPGA
Laboratory exercises on CAD usage for microcontrollers
Microcontroller as the heart of the Embedded system
Standard peripherals like UART, SPI, Bidirectional parallel bus, ADC
Decoding circuits and junction and MOS memory matrix
Static RAMs, elementary cells and organization
Static RAMs, elementary cell and sensing amplifier circuit
SDRAM and DDR memories, operation logic
Dual-port memories, elementary cell, pin-out and operation logic
FIFO memories, architecture, status flags and operation logic
Access and timing for ROM and RAM memories, in read and write
Overview of latest technologies: Ferroelectric RAM (FeRAM), Hybrid Memory Cube (HMC), Phase Change Memory (PCM), Memristor memories
Logic networks for programmable circuits: review of Boolean algebra and analysis and synthesis of combinational and sequential circuits
Hazards and techniques to avoid them
Synthesis of a network on a given architecture
CPLD and FPGA: Detailed architecture of a commercial device from the Altera MAX3000 family
Implementation of combinational circuits like Multiplexers, Demultiplexers, Comparators, Encoders, Decoders
Implementation of sequential circuits and state machines
Rules to follow and typical errors
CAD applied to programmable circuits: Top-Down design technique, Schematic Entry, Simulation, Constraints, Fitting, Configuration
Students will apply what they have learned in the course
Working in small groups, they will use Quartus prime and STM32CubeIde CADs with a microcontroller development board and an FPGA board
Students will develop small projects to decode signals, drive displays, read buttons, etc.

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (first available session after course end)

assessment_rules: The assessment verifies knowledge and understanding through open questions, ability to apply knowledge and understanding through exercises (logic network synthesis/analysis, VHDL code, CAD usage for projects, microcontroller solutions), autonomy of judgment through exercises on simple projects involving autonomous choices, communicative abilities through proper use of technical language, and learning ability through questions on laboratory activity. Grading is based on a scale from Insufficient to 30 e Lode. A minimum of 18 is required for a passing grade, indicating elementary knowledge and ability to handle simple tasks. Excellent grades (29-30 e Lode) signify complete, in-depth knowledge, autonomous and flexible operation, and critical abilities.
